title: Dynamic Topic Modeling for Cross-Corpus Temporal Analysis
read_from: arXiv preprint (states CIKM '26 and DOI on first page)
subcategory: cross-corpus dynamic embedded topic model with shared backbone
task: Comparing topic trajectories over time across several corpora
problem: Topics learned independently per corpus and aligned post hoc do not keep stable correspondence across corpora and time.
architecture: A D-ETM shared backbone is trained on the merged multi-corpus collection; then, with the backbone frozen, corpus-specific residual offsets to topic embeddings are learned (with anchor and smoothness regularisers), keeping one shared topic index across corpora.

datasets.name: COHA
datasets.details: Magazine and News genres, downsampled (rho = 0.3); 40,501 chunks

baselines: independent D-ETM per corpus (own or merged vocabulary)
key_results: Trajectory Retrieval@1 97.5% with residual adaptation vs 17.9% with full fine-tuning; same-index trajectory JSD 0.169 vs 0.586.
Held-out perplexity on HBR 2,396.78 (residual adaptation) vs 2,479.74 (independent) and 2,127.39 (full fine-tuning).
strengths: Builds cross-corpus alignment into training instead of post-hoc matching.

limitations.text: Full fine-tuning gives better perplexity and topic quality; on COHA residual adaptation has worse perplexity than independent models.
Human assessment of interpretability and other corpus combinations are left for future work.

notes: K = 20; code URL is truncated in the PDF text.
